Research programme

A research library with visible verification limits.

A maintained source collection and design record, paired with small working implementations and explicit evidence boundaries.

Research informs engineering; it does not substitute for it

The repository currently maintains a 162-entry bibliography, a literature review, design decisions, open questions and a reproducible benchmark methodology.

Applied

Compiler and language design

The implementation uses established compiler, typing, IR and VM principles; no formal soundness proof is claimed.

Small reverse-mode engine

Differentiable programming

The tensor tape and finite-difference tests are a compact implementation, not an MLIR/JAX-scale compiler.

Documented approximations

Numerical and visual methods

Floating-point deviations, 4×4 coverage sampling, Oklab colour utilities and artistic fBm are described in project docs.

Open research

AI safety and agents

Reasoning, planning, multimodal agents, interpretability and safety remain research questions—not shipped capabilities.

Source library and verification status

The bibliography file records 162 entries spanning programming languages, compilers, differentiable programming, numerical methods, graphics, security and evaluation.

The current build environment does not permit direct access to arXiv or publisher hosts. Do not treat every identifier in the inherited bibliography as externally verified; the research README records that limitation.

Open research/references.bibOpen CPython architectural analysisOpen literature review and limitationsOpen benchmark methodology

Research questions become implementation decisions

The next semantic migration is executed as shadow probes against the Python reference: retain the oracle, compare valid and invalid programs, and keep production semantics switched on until parity gates pass.

No fabricated numbers

Evidence is scoped

Checked-in benchmarks describe a small reference machine and are not comparative performance claims.

Negative results count

Limitations are recorded

The project labels CPU-only, unsupported GPU, incomplete frontends and platform gaps explicitly.

No AGI guarantee

Research remains open

AGI is an open research objective; no consequence is promised by the language or current implementation.

PEACOCK AI

Experimental language and ecosystem. Status is evidence-led, not a release claim.
